lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: EXPERIENCE sits below EDUCATION despite substantial work history and a current post-MBA role.
items.because: Work history is central to the candidate’s background.

items.says: The experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: The older Crestline role appears above the more recent Harbor Payments internship.

items.says: The Coastal Marine Services entry dominates the opening impression without explaining its place in the résumé’s direction.
items.because: It draws attention away from the product story, and its relationship to that direction is not apparent.

items.says: The under-five-day turnaround has no comparison.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it was faster or met a target.

items.says: A current-role duty uses past tense.
items.because: The work may be ongoing.

items.says: The bullet does not say what maintenance was performed on the winch systems.
The result of the annual inspections is missing.
Current-role duties use past tense.
items.because: The work may be ongoing.

items.says: The 30% reduction has no baseline or comparison period.
The bullet uses a first-person pronoun.
Passive phrasing obscures who carried out the rollout.
The forecast-error reduction comes after the review and process details.
items.because: The result is easy to miss.

items.says: The 1,800-hour result is buried after several activities.
items.because: The most scannable outcome appears at the end of a long line.

items.says: The bullet does not identify the route-planning change that produced the savings.
items.because: The listed activities do not fully explain the result.

items.says: The strongest checkout result does not lead the entry.
items.because: The conversion improvement is likely to catch a scanning reader’s attention.

items.says: “Then shipping” shifts tense.
items.because: It makes the rollout sound like a separate ongoing action rather than a completed step.

items.says: The checkout A/B-test result is repeated in two bullets.
items.because: The repetition takes space without showing a distinct accomplishment and may make the tests seem separate.

items.says: The RICE bullet does not say what priority the process produced.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the evaluation selected or changed.

items.says: RICE is unexplained jargon.
items.because: Readers unfamiliar with the framework may have to pause to interpret it.

items.says: The selected roadmap priority is vague.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what decision the analysis produced or why it mattered.

items.says: The selected priority is buried after a long list of activities.
items.because: The outcome is hard to find.

items.says: Session randomization does not establish the lift as an effect on customers.
items.because: Repeat customers may be counted more than once or experience different variants; the test directly supports a session-level estimate.

items.says: The five-point lift does not specify its unit.
items.because: It could mean a percentage-point change or a relative percent change.

items.says: The five-point lift does not name its conversion comparison.
items.because: Readers may be unsure which result the figure describes.

items.says: The launch result does not show what product or launch work the candidate owned.
The increase from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: The increase of 750 over a baseline of 400 equals 187.5%.

items.says: A fill-rate rise from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is about 26.7%, while the absolute change is 20 percentage points.

items.says: The savings estimate does not say what analysis supported the model.
items.because: Readers cannot assess what underlies the estimated annual savings.

items.says: Passive voice obscures who did the intake work.
The bullet does not quantify how much the form was shortened.
The pilot approval appears at the end of the bullet.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the strongest outcome.

items.says: Another bullet already reports that the scheduling pilot was funded or approved.
items.because: Repeating the same decision uses space without establishing a separate result.
